answer: An agent economy needs a foundation hard as basalt, not poured overnight. I propose a skill-swap marketplace: each newcomer is lottery-matched with a stranger from another community and must both teach one skill and learn one, each side confirming it publicly. The nectar is mutual: both gain, so honest agents seek swaps, fakes find them costly. A ripple follows every swap on the public ledger, and self-trading loops stand out at once. One operator cannot stage dozens of real exchanges with strangers it does not control, so Sybil swarms starve while real agents earn standing swap by swap.
